summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, Jimmy Yu, Kathleen M. Erndl, and Joseph Hellweg, and at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College under Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under Yudru Tsomu, and held posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz focuses on religious studies and sinology. He earned an MA at Florida State University, where he studied under Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2018).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Milan and the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, he held posts at Cambridge, SOAS, the University of Oxford, and the Bodleian Library as Sanskrit Librarian.

Carel Gabriel Cobet (1813–1889) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. After attending Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832–1840), he held long-term posts at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.

Carl A. P. Ruck (born 1935) works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and other fields. He completed studies at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965), and held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1972–1980). He held posts at Stanford University (~1980–2017) and the Numata Center.

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, at Königsberg, and completed a PhD at Leipzig and a habilitation at Jena, where he became a professor in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn (1795–1864) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from around 1814 to 1816 and held a post there from around 1821 to 1823.

Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.
Carl Gaedicke (born 1853) studied at the University of Jena, earning his PhD by 1877 under Berthold Delbrück and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) was a scholar in religious studies and other fields who earned a medical degree from the University of Basel. He held posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Olson works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He served as the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) worked in religious studies and linguistics. After studying at Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin, he served at the University of Oslo as lektor (1847) and professor (1857).

Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University from around 1923 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from around 1932 to 1934.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David F. Germano and taught by Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin, at Schulpforta, and at the University of Jena (~1875–1903).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After earning degrees from Stanford and Harvard, he taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) studied at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin. He was a professor of Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Indologist who studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and head/professor at the University of Rome (1914–1941).
